tasks.question: 'Living in a city is better than living in the countryside.' How far do you agree?

cues.cue: cities / better / but / countryside / has charm
models: I partly agree that cities are better, because they offer more opportunities, although it is also true that the countryside has its own charm.

cues.cue: cities / offer / more jobs / but / cost more
models: While I agree to some extent that cities offer more jobs, I also think that they cost more, which complicates the picture.

cues.cue: cities / offer / convenience / but / can feel impersonal
models: Although this may be true that cities offer convenience, it is important to consider that they can feel impersonal, since community ties are often weaker.

cues.cue: cities / provide / better healthcare / but / countryside / offers cleaner air
models: There is some truth in the idea that cities provide better healthcare, however the countryside offers cleaner air, and this changes things because health depends on more than hospitals.

cues.cue: city life / exciting / but / countryside / peaceful
models: I can understand both sides of the argument, since city life is exciting, and yet the countryside offers real peace.

cues.cue: cities / connect / people / but / can feel crowded
models: This argument has some merits; however, cities can feel overcrowded, it overlooks the fact that some people thrive on that energy, which means the debate isn't one-sided.

tasks.question: 'Technology has done more good than harm.' To what extent do you agree?

models: I partly agree that technology saves time, because it automates many tasks, although it is also true that it can cause dependency.

cues.cue: technology / connect / people / but / reduce / face-to-face contact
models: Although this may be true that technology connects people, it is important to consider that it reduces face-to-face contact, since real relationships still need presence.

models: There is some truth in the idea that technology improves productivity, however it also increases screen time, and this changes things because health can suffer as a result.

models: I agree in part, but I also believe that technology removes privacy, and this cannot be ignored because personal data is now widely shared.

models: While this is valid in some cases, such as technology benefiting education, it does not apply when schools lack the resources to use it well, and therefore access remains unequal.
